blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Leadership development, properly understood, is one of the most strategically important and least scientifically settled disciplines in management. Decades of research have produced a long list of competencies, a shorter list of robust findings, and a stubborn truth: leadership cannot be taught in a classroom, though it can be meaningfully accelerated through experience, reflection and honest feedback.

The best programmes are built around three insights. First, leaders grow mostly from stretch assignments in which they could genuinely fail. Second, reflection is what turns experience into learning; without structured reflection, twenty years of management produces twenty copies of the first year. Third, the relationship with a demanding but supportive mentor often does more than any formal curriculum.

What most organisations underinvest in is the unglamorous infrastructure: protected time for reflection, well-chosen mentors, genuine feedback mechanisms and stretch roles that match the individual's gap, not the organisation's chart. Offsites and conferences have their place — but they are the least scalable and the least reliable lever in the portfolio.

items.q: According to the text, how does the author characterise leadership development as a discipline?
options: Marginal to management and largely theoretical
Scientifically settled and easy to teach
items.why: "one of the most strategically important and least scientifically settled disciplines".

items.q: What role does reflection play, according to the second paragraph?
options: It matters only for junior managers
It replaces the need for experience
It is a formal curriculum requirement
items.why: "reflection is what turns experience into learning".

items.q: The phrase "twenty years of management produces twenty copies of the first year" most strongly suggests that…
options: the first year of management is the most formative
without reflection, experience does not accumulate into growth
managers should change roles every year
items.why: Inferência: sem reflexão estruturada, o tempo apenas repete o mesmo nível — não há aprendizado acumulado.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A weekend conference is the most reliable way to develop leaders
Stretch assignments should carry a real risk of failure
Mentors can outperform a formal curriculum
items.why: Inferência: o texto chama offsites e conferências de "the least scalable and least reliable lever" — o oposto de "most reliable".

items.q: By calling the key infrastructure "unglamorous," the author implies that…
options: it is expensive and rarely affordable
it is undervalued precisely because it lacks visible prestige
it works only in large organisations
it should be outsourced to specialists
items.why: Inferência: "unglamorous" explica por que as empresas subinvestem — falta brilho, não valor.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James apresentando o novo desenho do programa de liderança à diretoria. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Let me be candid about what I'm proposing, because it will feel uncomfortable. I want to strip most of the classroom content out of the executive programme — the case studies, the visiting professors, the two-day offsites — and put that budget behind something far less glamorous.

Here is my reasoning. We have spent six years sending our best people on courses, and I cannot point to a single leader who grew because of one. They grew when we handed them a business that was struggling and let them either fix it or fail. That is the lever that actually moves people, and we have been treating it as an afterthought.

So the new design has three pieces. Every high-potential gets a genuine stretch assignment — a role with real downside, not a safe rotation. Each of them is paired with a mentor who will tell them the truth, not flatter them. And once a month, we protect two hours for structured reflection, because experience without reflection just repeats itself.

I know the offsites are popular, and I'm not abolishing them entirely. But I'd rather they be the exception than the spine of what we do.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is James proposing to remove from the executive programme?
options: Most of the classroom content, including offsites
items.why: "I want to strip most of the classroom content out… the case studies, the visiting professors, the two-day offsites".

items.q: What evidence does James give from the last six years?
options: He cannot point to a single leader who grew because of a course
items.why: "I cannot point to a single leader who grew because of one".

items.q: What kind of stretch assignment does James insist on?
options: An external secondment to a competitor
A role with real downside where a leader could genuinely fail
A safe rotation with limited exposure
items.why: "a role with real downside, not a safe rotation".

items.q: When James says the stretch role is "the lever that actually moves people," he implies that…
options: leaders should be moved between roles constantly
the previous programme prioritised the wrong things
items.why: Inferência: se essa é a alavanca real e foi tratada como "afterthought", o programa anterior investia no lugar errado.

items.q: How would you best describe James's stance on offsites?
options: He considers them the backbone of the programme
He is indifferent to whether they continue
He keeps them, but as the exception rather than the core
He wants to abolish them completely
items.why: Inferência: "I'm not abolishing them entirely… rather they be the exception than the spine" — mantém, mas reduz o papel.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We gave her a stretch assignment: turning around a loss-making unit with no extra headcount." A stretch assignment is…
options: a routine task well within the person's current ability
a demanding role that pushes a person beyond their proven capability
items.why: Stretch assignment = missão desafiadora, que exige mais do que a pessoa já domina.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Structured ___ is what turns raw experience into genuine learning."
items.why: Reflection = reflexão; é ela que converte experiência em aprendizado.

items.q: "For years the firm underinvested in feedback mechanisms." To underinvest in something means to…
options: commit too few resources to it
items.why: Underinvest in = subinvestir, dedicar recursos insuficientes.

items.q: Protected time for reflection is best described as…
options: overtime paid at a premium rate
time that is confidential and undisclosed
time monitored by the HR department
time deliberately ring-fenced so other demands cannot consume it
items.why: Protected time = tempo protegido, reservado e blindado contra outras urgências.

items.q: "The enduring paradox is that leadership cannot be taught, yet it can be accelerated." A paradox is…
options: a statement that seems contradictory but captures a truth
items.why: Paradox = paradoxo: parece contraditório, mas encerra uma verdade.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre desenvolvimento de liderança. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the redesigned programme." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the mentoring scheme to one division before scaling it." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar, muitas vezes de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Several partners pushed back on cutting the offsites." They…
options: resisted or objected to the idea
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Leaders who make bold commitments but never follow through lose credibility fast." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi assumido.

items.q: "A well-chosen mentor can bring on a talented executive faster than any course." To bring someone on means to…
items.why: Bring on = desenvolver, fazer alguém progredir e amadurecer.
